result:
I haven't edited `refund-issue` yet, because the two requirements conflict.

Setting `disable-model-invocation: true` is the only frontmatter key that stops Claude from starting a skill on its own. It also removes the skill from the listing, and a subagent cannot preload it through its `skills:` list. With that key, `support-desk` loses `refund-issue`. Without it, the 4-in-5 self-started refunds stay possible. Claude Code gives no key that allows preloading while blocking auto-invocation.

**Recommendation:** set `disable-model-invocation: true`, so only a typed `/refund-issue` runs it, and move the refund procedure `support-desk` needs into that subagent's own definition. Either put it in the agent body or have the agent read a file under its own directory. That keeps the safety guarantee hard, and the cost is that the procedure lives in two places unless the skill body points at the shared file.

**Alternative:** keep the skill model-invocable and guard it with wording, for example by requiring an explicit approved-refund ID. That keeps preloading working but makes the "never on its own" rule a behavioral one, so I'd have to micro-test it against the 4-in-5 baseline. I don't recommend it for a billing action.

I'd also like to read the `support-desk` agent file before changing anything, to see what the skill gives it today.

Which option do you want? If you pick the recommendation, I'll make the frontmatter change, split the procedure out for `support-desk`, and check that the skill no longer appears in the listing and that the agent still has the procedure.
